issues.problem: The partition ellipse is drawn through the offset-number row, so the stroke strikes out '2-3-4' and '7-8-9' at both widths. The step-2 label '(2) deleted' sits on offset 3 and runs into the '↑ pulls 3–5' label next to it. The labels collide, and the numbers the step text refers to (3 to 5, 6 to 8) are the hardest ones to read.
issues.fix: Make the ellipse only as tall as the boxes, or drop it and use a plain bracket, and put the offset numbers fully below it. Move '(2) deleted' under offsets 0–2 (the struck boxes) and keep '↑ pulls 3–5' under offset 4 with at least 8px between the two.

issues.problem: On phone the panel titles 'a · a persistent connection, in chunks', 'b · through the API server' and 'c · a dedicated upload service' come after each drawing and have a rule under them. They read as headings of the next drawing: 'a' appears to label the through-API panel, and 'c' sits at the bottom with nothing under it. The italic note 'must be synchronous: users want to see it now' also runs into the photo chip at the top left of panel 2.
issues.fix: Put each title above its drawing (title, rule, drawing, notes), the same as the desktop version and the sample's panel titles. Move the 'must be synchronous' note below the drawing, or indent it so it clears the chip.

issues.problem: Phone step-throughs reserve the height of the final step from step 1 on. In fig-10a step 1 there are about 300px of empty grid between the one drawn row and Prev/Next, so the drawing and its step sentence are far apart. This is the same problem as lec01 critic #6.
issues.fix: Use the lec01 fix: on phone, crop the viewBox to the rows up to the current step (or shorten the reserved height), so Prev/Next and the step text sit right under the part that just changed.

issues.problem: These are figure deserts. §10.5 'More servers, or faster code?' runs about five desktop screens with no figure, only prose, a cross-reference chip and a cProfile code block. In §3.5, after fig-3d, there are three screens of prose and a 'More precisely' box (CDN egress, how the CDN reads a private bucket, SigV4). The sample's rhythm is paragraph, figure, paragraph, and these runs are walls of text.
issues.fix: §10.5: add a small figure of the 90/10 canary split (load balancer → 90% plain servers, 10% profiled canary → flame bars showing 'one function = most of the time'). §3.5: add a one-row sketch of 's3://insta-images/<user_id>/<image_id>' with the bucket swapped for the CDN host, so the 'plain string concatenation' point is drawn. Alternatively, move part of the CDN-reads-private-bucket prose into fig-3d's caption.

issues.problem: The overview page's hand-off reads '← Previous chapter · 9 · What to keep'. This page is the lecture's opening, so the link actually goes to the previous lecture's last chapter, but it is labelled as a chapter of this lecture (and Lecture 07 has 11 chapters). The reader cannot tell which lecture it belongs to.
issues.fix: On overview pages, label the back link 'Previous lecture' and name it 'Lecture 06 · Minting unique IDs', matching the 'Next lecture → Lecture 08 · …' link at the end of chapter 11.

issues.problem: Clip 5·1 is not drawn by the same hand as the other figures. Its desktop lettering is about 18–22px with heavy strokes ('The CDN checks the URL, not the person.' is about 22px), while the static figures and the other three clips letter at about 13–15px. The stage is also only about 540px wide inside a 920px sheet, so it reads as a different, zoomed-in drawing. 'GET /users/A/posts' fades to pale blue in the poster and looks disabled.
issues.fix: Rescale the composition so lettering lands at 15–16px on desktop, the same as Clips 2·1, 3·1 and 8·1 (lec01 critic #3 rule), and give the stage the same sheet width as the other clips. Keep 'GET /users/A/posts' at full request blue in the poster, because it is the step that decides who gets the URL.

issues.problem: In the portrait layout the 'post_publish key: user_id' label sits on top of the stream cylinder's top outline, and the cylinder is cut off by the top of the stage.
issues.fix: Shift the stream down about 24px in the phone composition, or put the label above the stage padding, so the label and the cylinder outline don't touch.

issues.where: 5-privacy aside 'The instructor's DRM' (sweep/1440-light/5-privacy/011.png); §10.5 'The instructor used it recently for a couple of cases' (sweep/1440-light/10-running-the-pipeline/014.png)
issues.problem: Teacher-biography voice is back (lec01 critic #14): an aside is titled after the instructor, and 'The instructor used it recently…' and 'According to the lecture, Instagram uses cProfile…' read like a summary of a recording, not a written page.
issues.fix: Retitle the aside by its subject (for example 'DRM, for paid content'). Turn the cProfile sentences into plain claims: 'cProfile is fine on a laptop or a canary; Instagram has written about running it on one production server', with the source link.

issues.problem: The verdict copy is question-specific and agrees with the reveal, which is good. But on every card the right answer is the second button, and it is always the hedged option ('It depends on what the page shows', 'Only if you configure it to'). After two cards the reader can guess without thinking.
issues.fix: Vary the position of the correct option, and on at least a third of the cards make the correct option a plain, definite statement.

issues.problem: The comment '# on a laptop or a canary, not the whole …' runs past the right edge of the code block at 1440 and is cut off mid-word.
issues.fix: Break the comment onto its own line above the call, or wrap long comment lines in code blocks.

issues.problem: Some labels are ambiguous. In fig-6a 'key: user_id' floats between the analytics and feed pull arrows, so it reads as a property of one consumer, not of the topic. In fig-9b 'won't count' on the hashtag api → cache arrow reads as 'the cache won't count'; the board meant the cache is optional and holds no counts.
issues.fix: fig-6a: put 'key: user_id' directly under the kafka label, as fig-8c does. fig-9b: relabel it 'optional' (as fig-9a does) or 'cache: optional'.
